commit.subject: feat(viewer): commands whose exit code was not recorded show as unknown

entries.text: Coordinator decision on your F2 question: readability wins. Keep the read/search/test/etc. kind and the real command title for commands run inside code-mode scripts whose exit code wasn't printed, and give them a new 'unknown' status (domain model, normalize, UI: a neutral marker distinct from ok/failed/running, legend/tooltip 'exit code not recorded'; filters such as 'failures only' must treat unknown as not failed). Keep the explicit failed/ok when the script printed the exit code. The checkout is now on fix/ledger-review (7 ledger fixes by another agent on top of your fix/codex-review); create branch fix/unknown-status from it. Also fix the empty 'fetch ' title for web actions with no URL. Check 019f7548 in the UI again (server on PORT=4781, stop only your PID). Same verification and commit rules. Report commits, verification, and the before/after lane counts for 019f7548.
Both committed. Build, start the server on 4781, and check `019f7548` after the change plus a full sweep:

entries.text:
Ah, I see the issue — the dashed border is applying to the whole row because the status class gets shared between the row and my marker styling. I'll rename the marker class to "exit-unknown" to scope it properly and avoid clashing with the row-level class.

Since the feature commit isn't HEAD, I'll fold this small fix into it using a fixup commit followed by a non-interactive autosquash rebase rather than trying to edit interactively.



I spotted a CSS conflict: since rows carry status as a class, my `.unknown` style is also applying its dashed outline to the whole `exit ?` row instead of just the marker. I'll rename the marker class to fix it.
